reasons: Classification is correct: Article XIII(b) caps only Licensor at one half of amounts paid and leaves Licensee entirely uncapped, which is expressly walk-away territory under LOL-CAP (customer uncapped / vendor cap below six months' fees), and there are no carve-outs — a genuine critical deviation, not an acceptable fallback.

The redline reaches the playbook position: the cap is made mutual at the greater of 12 months' fees paid or payable and USD 1,000,000, the consequential-damages exclusion is mutualized, the standard uncapped Excluded Claims set is added, and Licensee's fee obligations are excluded from the cap — consistent with the model language and directionally correct for the customer.

Edits stay within the existing Article XIII sentences rather than rewriting the section; the high changed-character ratio flagged by the advisory check is inherent to mutualizing a one-sided cap and exclusion, so it does not indicate over-editing.

Comment is accurate, concise and in the required voice: it states what changed, why the Licensor-only half-of-fees cap falls below the position, and that indemnities/confidentiality sit outside the cap.

Minor residual gap worth noting to the drafter (not a basis for failure): the tail of paragraph (a) still reads "UNDER NO CIRCUMSTANCE SHALL LICENSOR BE LIABLE ... FOR ANY INFRINGEMENT ...", a Licensor-only IP disclaimer that sits in tension with the new Excluded Claims and may need cleanup under the IP indemnity rule.
